title: Freezing Tissue in OCT using Isopentane
author: Liz Tuck
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x3wfqpe
materials: Put lumps of dry ice into the iso-pentane and monitor with the -100⁰C thermometer until it measures -70°C.

steps.title: Prepare isopentane bath
steps.instruction: In a fume hood or down‑flow table, wear appropriate PPE, place a metal container on dry ice and half‑fill it with isopentane enough to completely immerse the tissue pieces; the isopentane will be chilled to about –70 °C.

steps.title: Cool forceps and ready cryotube
steps.instruction: Cool one pair of forceps on the dry ice, keep the second pair at room temperature, and (if used) place a labelled cryotube on dry ice.

steps.title: Label cryomold and foil
steps.instruction: Write the sample ID on the cryomold and on a piece of foil.

steps.title: Trim tissue to size
steps.instruction: Trim the tissue into a piece small enough to fit into the cryomold (maximum 10 × 10 mm for spatial transcriptomics).

steps.title: Add OCT and position tissue
steps.instruction: Half‑fill the cryomold with OCT, place the tissue inside, ensure correct orientation (region of interest facing down), and make sure a thin OCT layer covers the bottom so the tissue is fully covered.

steps.title: Cover tissue with OCT
steps.instruction: Add more OCT if needed to ensure the tissue is completely submerged and covered.

steps.title: Freeze in isopentane
steps.instruction: Using the cooled forceps, submerge the cryomold in the isopentane bath (≈ –70 °C) until the sample is completely frozen.

steps.title: Wrap frozen sample
steps.instruction: When fully frozen, wrap the cryomold (still containing the sample) in foil and keep on dry ice; alternatively, remove the sample from the cryomold and place it in a labelled cryotube on dry ice.

steps.title: Store at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer the foil‑wrapped (or cryotube) samples on dry ice to a labelled box and store the box in a –80 °C freezer.

steps.title: Monitor isopentane temperature
steps.instruction: If processing additional samples, continuously monitor the isopentane temperature and adjust the dry‑ice amount as necessary to maintain ≈ –70 °C.

steps.title: Dispose or recycle isopentane
steps.instruction: Wearing cold‑resistant gloves, remove the metal container from the dry ice. Let the isopentane and dry ice evaporate in a fume hood with the lid off, or warm the isopentane to –10 °C, decant it into a labelled bottle, keep the bottle in a fume hood with the lid loosened until it reaches room temperature.
